items.title: Advertisers stay responsible when AI agents run campaigns, UK's ICO says
items.excerpt: A 51-page ICO adtech report says advertisers remain accountable when AI agents run their campaigns, and health inferences drawn from chatbot prompts count as sensitive data needing explicit consent.
items.rationale: New regulator report that directly sets accountability for agent-run ad buying and limits targeting on chatbot-prompt inferences; distinct from the ICO's 11-25 Muse statement run in politics.

items.title: Microsoft Advertising ads in Bing AI Mode getting harder to see
items.excerpt: Microsoft Advertising's ads inside Bing AI Mode results now blend more closely with organic answers, with near-invisible sponsored labels, making paid placements in the AI answer surface harder for users to distinguish.
items.rationale: New ad-format change on an AI answer surface (paid placement blending into answers) — a concrete inventory change for search buyers, separate from the 11-21 'Made with AI' label item.

items.title: Businesses stay liable for what their AI agents tell shoppers, ACCC says
items.excerpt: Australia's ACCC told Black Friday shoppers businesses remain liable for what their AI shopping agents say, naming Meta Muse, ChatGPT dots and Google Tasks; a full ACCC report on AI shopping agents is due within months.
items.rationale: Consumer-law regulator's on-record position on seller liability for AI shopping-agent claims during Black Friday, with a forthcoming report flagged; not previously covered in any section.

items.title: Agentic shopping falls short as AI recommends out-of-stock products
items.excerpt: ob.session sent ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude shopping for a fictional UK shopper; across 400+ links only 35% were in stock. ChatGPT delivered a usable item 45% of the time, Gemini 33%, Claude 21%.
items.rationale: Fresh test data (35% in-stock across 400+ links, per-assistant hit rates) that tells merchants why product-feed freshness decides AI-agent sales; a different study from the 11-26 SEJ fake-deal test.

items.title: Shopify Gives Merchants Proof to Fight Agentic Order Chargebacks
items.excerpt: Shopify now gives merchants more evidence for chargebacks on orders placed by AI agents, per a Nov. 25 changelog entry, ahead of Black Friday-Cyber Monday agentic orders.
items.rationale: New Shopify release (Nov. 25 changelog) that protects sales placed by AI agents ahead of BFCM; a different feature from the 11-02 agent-referral payment program.
